question: In which year was India’s first paperless budget presented in the Parliament?
solution:
The correct answer is__** 2021**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's first paperless budget was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on February 1, 2021.**
 
• Owing to the COVID-19 pandemic,** the traditional 'budget bahi khata' was replaced by a 'Made in India' tablet.**
 
• The tradition of presenting a paperless budget in the Parliament was initiated in 2021, in light of the coronavirus pandemic and as a measure of digital progression.
 
• This marked a significant step in the ongoing digital revolution and was seen as an effort towards creating a more sustainable and environmentally friendly workflow within the government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Union Budget of a country is a comprehensive **annual financial statement** outlining the government's estimated revenue from taxes and expenditures for the forthcoming fiscal year.
 
• It details the financial plan involving two main components: **revenue and expenditure.**
 
• The revenue budget includes tax income and other types of revenue, while the expenditure budget is the estimate of total spending, categorized into plan (for growth, development, and welfare measures) and non-plan expenditures (for the everyday running of state departments).
 
• The Budget also serves as a policy document, as it discloses the government's vision, indicating areas where expenses will increase or decrease.
 
• The budgetary process involves various stages: **preparation, presentation, approval (by houses of Parliament), implementation, and auditing (by the Comptroller and Auditor General).**
 
• Being a strategic tool of governance, the Budget impacts all segments of the economy and society, inducing implications for fiscal policy, public finance, inflation, the business environment, and the common man's day-to-day life.
